stories.claim: Alaska's HB 239, criminalizing AI-generated CSAM, became law without the governor's signature; passed Senate 20-0 / House 39-1 (May 19-20); not among the nine bills vetoed June 18.
Per a June 18 Landye Bennett Blumstein analysis, Alaska has no statewide data-center regulatory framework; SB 250 (grid-cost protection) died in committee in May.
The Saving the OOI Act (S.4822) passed the U.S. Senate by voice vote June 17; NSF reversed course to preserve the ~900-instrument OOI array, including Gulf of Alaska sensors.

Alaska's first-year CMS Rural Health Transformation allocation is ~$272M (among the two largest state shares); ~400 projects advanced from ~1,800; full applications due June 22, awards in July; Rep. Genevieve Mina said the federal design is 'almost directing us to AI'.
The Alaska House rejected the Senate's LNG tax bill 28-12 on June 20; a conference committee targets July 1.

stories.claim: A proposed $500M North Slope AI data-center campus (Stak Energy) with on-site gas generation received a state preliminary approval to lease.

note: Cited sources total: 5 in-text stories plus 1 background reference. Validator (Phase 3) verified all; several AK outlet URLs (Alaska Beacon, CBC, akleg.gov, AK DOH) 403'd at validation and affected claims were stripped or attributed to the corroborating fetched source. HB 239 felony-class language, CMS 22% figure, GVEA rate figure, and STAK in-window CBC claims were stripped.
